sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Average Annual Precipitation**: India receives about 4,000 billion cubic meters (BCM) of precipitation annually, out of which surface water availability is estimated at **1,869 BCM**.
• **Utilizable Water Resource**: Due to topographical, hydrological, and technological constraints, only about **1,123 BCM** (690 BCM from surface water and 433 BCM from groundwater) can be put to beneficial use.
• **Spatial Disparity**: Water availability varies heavily; regions like the Brahmaputra and Barak basin have high abundance, while the Pennar and Sabarmati basins face acute structural scarcity.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Per capita water availability is declining progressively due to population explosion, pushing India towards **water stress** (below 1,700 cubic meters/person/year) and nearing **water scarcity** (below 1,000 cubic meters/person/year).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix

items.definition: A river basin is the entire geographical area drained by a river and its tributaries, whereas a catchment refers specifically to the area that collects rainwater and drains it into a specific water body or reservoir.
The ratio of water effectively used by crops to the total water diverted or withdrawn from surface sources; traditionally very low in Indian flood irrigation systems (~35-40%).
CWC is the apex technical organization in India for initiating, coordinating, and furthering schemes for control, conservation, and utilization of water resources.

items.term: National Water Policy & Inter-State River Water Disputes Act
items.definition: Formulates broad national guidelines for water allocation priorities (Drinking water first, followed by irrigation, hydropower, ecology, and agro-industries); disputes handled under Article 262 and specific tribunals.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Brahmaputra-Barak Basin**: Accounts for nearly 34% of the total national surface water resources despite a smaller geographical area share.
• **Ganga Basin**: The largest river basin in India by area, supporting over 40% of India's population, resulting in severe surface water stress and pollution loading.
• **Water Deficit Zones**: Western Rajasthan, Saurashtra, Kutch, and parts of the interior Deccan Plateau (Rayalaseema, Vidarbha).

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Heavy siltation of reservoirs, unscientific dam operations causing artificial floods, inter-state political friction, and severe industrial/sewage pollution.
• **Policy Interventions**: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY), Atal Bhujal Yojana, Jal Shakti Abhiyan ("Catch the Rain"), and the Interlinking of Rivers (ILR) project.

items.title: Mnemonic for National Water Policy Priority Order
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "D-I-H-E-A" (Drink Iron Hydros, Eat Apples)
• **Decoded Meaning**: 1. Drinking Water, 2. Irrigation, 3. Hydropower, 4. Ecology, 5. Agro-industries & Navigation.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates incorrect ranking options in policy-based MCQs.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: India has ~16% of the world's population, but only ~4% of the world's freshwater resources, and almost 80% of surface water is consumed by the agriculture sector alone.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states that 'Groundwater constitutes the majority of India's total water resource potential.' This is false; total precipitation and surface water potential (1,869 BCM) vastly exceeds total replenishable groundwater potential (~432 BCM).

Mains Value Addition: Use terms like 'Hydrological Poverty', 'Virtual Water Trade', 'Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM)', and quote Mihir Shah Committee recommendations on restructuring water governance bodies for exceptional marks.

keyTakeaways: India's surface water potential is heavily skewed geographically, with the Ganga and Brahmaputra-Barak basins holding the lions share.
Agriculture accounts for roughly 80% of total surface water withdrawal, making micro-irrigation and crop diversification imperative for water security.
Institutional mechanisms like CWC, Inter-State Water Disputes Tribunals, and National Water Policy govern surface water governance under constitutional federal provisions.
